Therefore its apparent meaning is definitely not intended. Abu Dawud's and Ibn Habib's interpretation of it is not agreed upon, so it cannot serve as proof. And Allah knows best.

Abu 'Umar said: Malik's proof is that they have agreed (ijma', scholarly consensus) that if a human being cannot be escaped (from), it is not slaughtered except by the means by which a controllable animal is slaughtered; then they differed, so it remains on its original ruling until they agree. This is not a proof, because their consensus was formed only concerning a controllable animal, and this is not controllable.

The Sixteenth issue: Among the completions of this topic is his saying, peace be upon him: "Indeed Allah has prescribed excellence (iḥsān) in all things. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let each of you sharpen his blade and let him spare his slaughtered animal." Narrated by Muslim from Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: "I memorized two things from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: 'Indeed Allah has prescribed...'" and he mentioned it.

Our scholars said: Excellence in slaughtering animals is gentleness toward them: one does not throw them down roughly, nor drag them from one place to another; sharpening the instrument; bringing the intention of permissibility and devotion (qurbah) and directing the animal toward the qiblah; hastening (ijhāz, to finish off a wounded animal quickly after having struck it), and cutting the two jugular veins (al-wadajayn) and the windpipe (al-ḥulqūm); letting it rest and leaving it until it cools; and acknowledging to Allah the favor, and thanking Him for the blessing, that He has subjected to us what, had He willed, He would have given power over us, and made lawful to us what, had He willed, He would have forbidden to us.

Rabi'ah said: Among the excellence of slaughter is that one does not slaughter an animal while another one is looking at it. Its permissibility is reported from Malik, and the first view is better.

As for the excellence of killing, it is general in everything, including ritual slaughter, retaliation (qiṣāṣ), prescribed punishments (ḥudūd), and other things. Abu Dawud narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Hurayrah, who both said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the shareetat al-shaytan," and Ibn 'Isa added in his narration: "(and it is that which is slaughtered so that it is cut but the jugular veins are not severed, then it is left and dies)."

The Seventeenth issue: His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿and what is sacrificed on the altars (nuṣub)﴾. Ibn Faris said: "Nuṣub" is a stone that used to be set up and worshipped, and the blood of slaughtered animals was poured on it, and it is also called naṣb. And al-Nasa'ib are stones set up around the rim of a well and made into supports, and a raised, standing dust. It was said: "Nuṣub" is a plural whose singular is niṣāb, like ḥimār and ḥumur. It was said: it is a singular noun and the plural is anṣāb, and they were three hundred and sixty stones. Ṭalḥah read "nuṣb" with the ṣād sukun. And it is reported from Ibn 'Umar "naṣb" with a fatḥah on the nūn and sukūn on the ṣād. Al-Jahdari (read it): with a fatḥah on the nūn and the ṣād, treating it as a singular noun like al-jabal and al-jamal, and its plural is anṣāb, like al-ajmāl and al-ajbāl.

Mujahid said: they are stones around Makkah on which they used to slaughter. Ibn Jurayj said: The Arabs used to slaughter in Makkah and sprinkle with blood whatever came near the House, and they would cut the meat and place it on the stones. When Islam came, the Muslims said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We have more right to honor this House with these acts," so it seems he, peace be upon him, did not dislike that, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Their flesh will not reach Allah, nor their blood, but what reaches Him is your piety﴾ [al-Hajj: 37]. And ﴿and what is sacrificed on the altars﴾ was revealed. The meaning is: the intention in it is glorifying the altars, not that slaughtering on them is permissible. [Note: in K and Z: because slaughtering on them is not permissible.]

Al-A'sha said:
"And the raised altar, do not sacrifice to it,
but worship your Lord, Allah."
[Note: "wa dhā al-naṣb" means "beware of and the raised altar."]

It was also said: "'alā" here means "li" (for), i.e., for their sake. Qutrub said. Ibn Zayd said: "what is sacrificed on the altars" and "what is dedicated to other than Allah" are one thing. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: what is sacrificed on the altars is a part of what is dedicated to other than Allah, but it was singled out for mention after its genus because of the prominence of the matter, the nobility of the place, and the people's veneration of it.

The Eighteenth issue: His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿and that you seek decision through the arrows﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it, and "an" is in the place of a nominative, meaning: and the seeking of decision (istiqsām) is forbidden to you. The arrows (al-azlām) are the gaming arrows (qidāḥ al-maysir), whose singular is zalam and zulum. He said:
"He spent the night dealing with them, a youth like the zalam."
Another said, using the plural:
"If Jadhimah has killed its nobles,
then its women strike with the arrows."
Muhammad ibn Jarir mentioned that Ibn Wakī' narrated to them from his father, from Sharik, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that the arrows are white pebbles with which they used to cast lots. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Sufyan ibn Wakī' told us: "They are chess." As for the verse of Labid:
"Its arrows slip from the dust..."
[Full line: "Until when the darkness was dispelled and it became bright, it set out early, its arrows slipping from the dust."]
They said he meant the hooves of the wild cow. The arrows of the Arabs are of three kinds: among them are the three that each person would take for himself, one of which says "do," another "do not," and the third is blank with nothing on it. He places them in a bag with him, and when he wants to do something he puts his hand in—they are identical—and whichever comes out he complies with and refrains according to what it indicates. If the blank arrow comes out, he repeats the drawing. This is the one with which Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum cast lots when he pursued the Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr at the time of the Hijrah. This practice was called istiqsām only because they used to seek by it their provision and what they wanted, as one says istisqā' for seeking rain. The analogue of what Allah, exalted is He, forbade is the saying of the astrologer: "Do not go out because of such-and-such star, and go out because of such-and-such star." And He, exalted and mighty, said: ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ [Luqman: 34]. This will be explained fully, Allah willing.

The second kind: seven arrows that were with Hubal inside the Ka'bah, on which was written what occurs among people of calamities; each arrow had a writing on it: one arrow had "the blood-money (diyah) of the intellect"; in another "from among you," in another "from other than you," and in another "attached" (mulṣaq), and on the rest were rulings concerning waters and other matters. With these Abd al-Muttalib cast lots over his sons, when he had vowed to sacrifice one of them if they reached ten: the well-known report recorded by Ibn Ishaq. These seven were also with every soothsayer (kāhin) and ruler of the Arabs, in the same manner as they were with Hubal in the Ka'bah. The third kind: the arrows of gambling (qidāḥ al-maysir), which are ten: seven of them have shares (ḥuẓūẓ), and three are blank (aghfāl). They used to cast with them for gambling, play, and amusement, and their wise men intended by them feeding the poor and the destitute in winter, in the time of cold and hardship and the inability to earn.

Mujahid said: "al-azlām" are the knucklebones (kiʿāb) of the Persians and Romans with which they gamble. Sufyan and Waki' said: they are chess. So seeking decision by all of this is seeking a share and portion, as we have explained, and it is among the consuming of wealth falsely, and it is forbidden. Every gambling with pigeons, dice, chess, or other such games is seeking decision by what is of the same meaning as the arrows, and all of it is forbidden; it is a form of soothsaying and claiming knowledge of the unseen. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: For this reason our companions forbade the matters that astrologers perform on the roads with the arrows they carry, and the slips of augury (riqā' al-fa'l), and the like. Ilkiya al-Tabari said: Allah forbade them only regarding matters of the unseen, for no soul knows what will befall it tomorrow, so the arrows have no effect in revealing the unseen. Some ignorant people deduced from this a refutation of al-Shafi'i's view on casting lots among slaves for manumission. This ignorant person did not know that what al-Shafi'i said is based on authentic reports, and it is not subject to objection by the prohibition of seeking decision by the arrows, for manumission is a legal ruling, and the Law may make the drawing of the lot a sign for establishing the ruling of manumission, definitively, to end disputes, or for an interest it sees. This is not equivalent to the statement of someone saying: "If you do such-and-such or say such-and-such, that will show you a matter in the future." So it is not permissible to make the drawing of the arrows a sign of something that will newly occur in the future, while it is permissible to make the drawing of the lot a definitive sign of manumission. Thus the difference between the two matters becomes clear.

The Nineteenth issue: Not among this category is seeking omens (ṭalab al-fa'l). The Prophet (ﷺ) liked to hear "O guided one! O successful one!" Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: "A sound gharib hadith." He liked the omen only because the soul is delighted by it and rejoices at the fulfillment of need and the attainment of hope, so the good opinion of Allah, exalted and mighty, becomes good, and He has said: "I am as My servant thinks of Me." The Prophet, peace be upon him, disliked tiyarah (bad omen), because it is among the practices of the people of shirk, and because it brings bad opinion of Allah, exalted and mighty. Al-Khattabi said: The difference between fa'l and tiyarah is that fa'l comes from the path of good opinion of Allah, while tiyarah comes from the path of relying on something other than Him. Al-Asma'i said: I asked Ibn 'Awn about fa'l, and he said: it is that a sick man hears "O Salim!" or that a seeker of a lost thing (al-bāghī) hears...

[Note: "al-bāghī" means the one who seeks a lost thing.]

...the one who hears (it), O (you) who finds [a meaning], and this is the meaning of the hadith of al-Tirmidhi. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "There is no *tiyara* (ill-omen taken from birds or events) and the best of it is *fa'l* (good omen)." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is *fa'l*?" He said: "A good word that one of you hears." More explanation of the meaning of *tiyara* will come, God willing.

It is related from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Knowledge is only by learning, and forbearance only by feigning forbearance. Whoever seeks good will be given it, and whoever guards against evil will be protected from it. Three people will not attain the high ranks: one who practises *kahana* (soothsaying), or one who seeks *istiqsam* (divination by arrows), or one who turns back from a journey because of *tiyara*."

The twentieth issue: the words of the Exalted: ﴿That is defiance (fisq)﴾ refer to seeking the decision by the arrows. *Fisq* means going out (of bounds), and it has been explained earlier. [[See vol. 1, p. 244 and what follows.]]

It has been said that it refers to all that was mentioned of treating as lawful all these prohibited things, and each of them is *fisq* and a going out from the lawful to the unlawful. Refraining from these prohibited things is part of fulfilling the contracts, since He says: "Fulfil the contracts" [Al-Ma'ida 5:1].

The twenty-first issue: the words of the Exalted: ﴿Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion﴾, meaning that they have despaired of your returning to their religion as disbelievers. Al-Dahhak said: This verse was revealed at the conquest of Makkah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah eight nights before the end of Ramadan in the ninth year, and it is said in the eighth year. When he entered it, the caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proclaimed: "Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' is safe; whoever lays down his weapons is safe; and whoever closes his door is safe."

In *ya'isa* there are two forms: *ya'isa yay'asu ya'san*, and *ayisa yay'isu ay'san* and *ay'asa*, as stated by al-Nadr ibn Shumayl.

﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾, meaning: do not fear them, but fear Me, for I am the One Able to grant you victory.

The twenty-second issue: the words of the Exalted: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾. This was because when the Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah, there was only the obligation of prayer; when he came to Madinah, Allah revealed the lawful and the unlawful until the Hajj. When he performed the Hajj and the religion was complete, this verse was revealed: "Today I have perfected your religion for you," and so on, as we shall explain.

The imams narrated on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: A man of the Jews came to Umar and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, there is a verse in your Book that you recite. If it had been revealed to us, the Jewish community, we would have taken that day as a festival." He said: "And which verse?" He said: "'Today I have perfected your religion for you, and completed My favour upon you, and I have approved Islam as your religion' [Al-Ma'ida 5:3]." Umar said: "Indeed I know the day on which it was revealed and the place in which it was revealed: it was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Arafat on a Friday." This is the wording of Muslim. In al-Nasa'i's version it is "on a Friday night." It is also related that when it was revealed on the Day of the Greater Hajj and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it, Umar wept. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "What makes you weep?" He said: "What made me weep is that we were in an increase of our religion, but now that it has been completed, nothing that is completed fails to decline." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "You have spoken truly."

Mujahid related that this verse was revealed on the day of the conquest of Makkah. I say: The first view is more sound, that it was revealed on a Friday, and it was the day of Arafat after the afternoon prayer, during the Farewell Pilgrimage in the tenth year, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing at Arafat on his she-camel al-Adba', so that the shoulder of the she-camel nearly split from its weight, and so she knelt down. [[From ja, ka and za. Al-Adba': the name of the she-camel of the Prophet (ﷺ).]] [[In za: "kādat" (nearly), which is the dialect of Tihama.]]

"Today" may be expressed by a part of it for the whole, and likewise a month by part of it, as you say: "We did such-and-such in the month of such-and-such, and in the year of such-and-such," while it is known that you did not occupy the whole month or the whole year. This is used in the speech of the Arabs and non-Arabs.

"Religion" is an expression for the laws which He legislated and opened for us, for they were revealed gradually, and the last of what was revealed was this verse, and no ruling was revealed after it. This was said by Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi. The majority said: what is meant is the greater part of the obligations and the permitting and forbidding. They said: Much Qur'an was revealed after that, including the verse on usury and the verse on *kalala* (inheritance), and so on. Rather, the greater part of the religion was completed and the matter of the Hajj, since no polytheist performed the circumambulation with them in that year, nor did anyone circumambulate the House naked, and all the people stood at Arafat.

It has also been said: "I have perfected your religion for you" means that I destroyed your enemy for you and made your religion prevail over every religion, just as you say: "What we want has been accomplished for us when your enemy has been dealt with."

The twenty-third issue: the words of the Exalted: ﴿And I have completed My favour upon you﴾, that is, by completing the laws and rulings and making the religion of Islam manifest, as I promised you when I said: "and that I may complete My favour upon you" [Al-Baqara 2:150]. It is the entry into Makkah safe and secure, and other things included in this upright creed, up to entry into the Garden in the mercy of Allah the Exalted.

The twenty-fourth issue: perhaps someone will say: the words of the Exalted: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾ indicate that the religion was not complete at some point in time, and that necessarily means that all those of the Muhajirun and the Ansar who died, and those who witnessed Badr and Hudaybiyya and pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in both pledges, and gave themselves for Allah along with the great trials that befell them, died upon an incomplete religion, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during that time was calling the people to an incomplete religion. It is known that incompleteness is a defect, and the religion of Allah the Exalted is upright, as He said: "a upright religion" [Al-An'am 6:161]. The answer is to be said to him: Why did you say that every deficiency is a defect, and what is your evidence for it? Then it is to be said to him: Tell me, does the shortness of the month become a defect? Is the shortening of the traveller's prayer a defect in it? Is the decrease of life, which Allah intended by His saying: "No one is granted a long life, nor is any of his life shortened" [Fatir 35:11], a defect in it? Is the shortness of the days of menstruation from what is customary, or the shortness of the days of pregnancy, or the loss of property by theft, fire or drowning, when its owner is not impoverished, a defect? So what do you deny about the deficiency of parts of the religion in the Law before the remaining parts are joined to it in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, being not a blemish or a defect? And what do you deny that the meaning of the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Today I have perfected your religion for you" may be understood in two ways?

One of them: that what is meant is that I have brought it to the furthest limit which it had with Me in what I decreed and determined. That does not necessarily mean that what came before that was deficient with a defect; rather, it may be described as a restricted deficiency, so it is said: it was deficient in comparison with what Allah the Exalted had in mind to join it to and to add to it. Like a man whom Allah allows to reach a hundred years, and it is said: Allah completed his life; and it does not follow from this that his life when he was sixty was deficient with a deficiency of inadequacy and flaw. For the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has been granted by Allah sixty years has left no excuse for himself regarding his lifespan." But it is permissible to describe it as a restricted deficiency, so it is said: it was deficient in comparison with what Allah the Exalted had in mind to bring it to and to extend it to. Allah has brought the noon, afternoon and night prayers to four rak'ahs; so if it is said at that point that He completed them, the statement would be correct, and it does not follow from this that when they were two rak'ahs they were deficient with a deficiency of inadequacy and flaw. Had it been said that they were deficient in comparison with what Allah had in mind to join to them and add to them, that would be correct. Likewise, this applies to the laws of Islam, and whatever was legislated of them bit by bit until Allah brought the religion to its final destination which it had with Him. And Allah knows best.

The other view: He meant by His saying "Today I have perfected your religion for you" that He granted them success in the Hajj, and that nothing else remained for them of the pillars of the religion. So they performed the Hajj, and the religion was thereby gathered together for them in the performance of its pillars and the upholding of its obligations. For he, upon him be peace, says: "Islam is built upon five" and so on. They had already bore witness, prayed, paid zakat, fasted, struggled, and performed umrah, but they had not performed Hajj. When they performed Hajj that day with the Prophet (ﷺ), Allah the Exalted revealed while they were at the standing place on the evening of Arafat: "Today I have perfected your religion for you, and I have completed My favour upon you." So what He meant was: He completed His setting of it for them. In this there is an indication that all acts of obedience are religion, faith and submission.

The twenty-fifth issue: the words of the Exalted: ﴿And I have approved Islam as your religion﴾, that is: I have informed you of My approval of it for you as a religion, for He, the Exalted, has always been pleased with Islam as a religion for us, so the specification of approval to that day would have no benefit if we took it according to its outward meaning. "Religion" (*dinan*) is in the accusative as a specification (*tamyiz*), and if you wish it may be the second object. It has been said: the meaning is "I am pleased with you when you submit to Me in the religion which I have legislated for you." It is also possible that He means: "I have approved Islam as your religion," that is, I have approved your submission in which you are today as a religion remaining in its perfection until the end of the verse, I will not abrogate anything from it. And Allah knows best. The word "Islam" in this verse is the same as in His saying: "Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam" [Al Imran 3:19], and it is what is explained in Jibril's question to the Prophet, upon both of them be prayers and peace: it is faith, deeds and branches.

The twenty-sixth issue: the words of the Exalted: ﴿But whoever is compelled by severe hunger﴾, meaning whoever is driven by necessity to eat carrion and the rest of the prohibited things in this verse. *Makhmasa* is hunger and the emptiness of the belly from food. *Al-khams* is the thinness of the belly. A man is *khamis* and *khumsan*, and a woman is *khamisa* and *khumsana*, and from this comes *akhmas al-qadam* (the arch of the foot). It is used frequently for hunger and emptiness. Al-A'sha said:

You spend the night in winter with your bellies full,
while your neighbours, hungry, spend the night emaciated.

That is: wrapped in hunger, their bellies having been made thin. And al-Nabigha said, describing the flatness of the belly from the side of its slenderness:

And the belly, with its folds, is flat and soft,
and the chest, its garment raised, with a breast set upright.

And in the hadith: "Light-bellied and dry-backed." *Khimas* is the plural of *khamis al-batn*, meaning slender-bellied. It informs that they were chaste regarding the property of people. From it also is the hadith: "Indeed the birds go out hungry and return full." *Al-khamisa* is also a garment; al-Asma'i said: *al-khama'is* are garments of silk or wool with markings, and they are black, and they were from the clothing of the people. The meaning of compulsion and its ruling has already been mentioned in al-Baqara.

The 27th issue: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿without inclining toward sin﴾, that is, not inclining toward what is forbidden. It has the same meaning as "neither transgressing nor exceeding" (Al-Baqarah 2:173), and that has already been discussed. Al-Janaf is inclining (al-mayl), and al-ithm is what is forbidden. From it is the saying of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "We did not incline toward it for sin," that is, we did not incline to it nor deliberately did it while knowing it. Every one who inclines is a mutajanif and janif. Al-Nakhaʿi, Yahya ibn Wththab and al-Sulami read mutajannif without an alif, and this is more emphatic in meaning, because the doubling of the letter ʿayn implies intensification and deepening of the meaning and firmness of its ruling. The form tafāʿala is only an imitation of a thing and approaching it. Do you not see that when you say "the branch swayed" (tamāyala al-ghusn), this implies swaying and near-inclination, whereas when you say "tamayyala," the ruling of inclination is established? Likewise, "tasāwana al-rajul" and "tasawwana," and "taʿāqala" and "taʿaqqala." So the meaning is: not deliberately intending disobedience in his purpose. This was said by Qatadah and al-Shafiʿi.

(Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful) That is, indeed Allah is, for him, Forgiving and Merciful, and the predicate was omitted. Sibawayh cited [a verse in rajaz by Abu al-Najm al-ʿIjli, whose wife was Umm al-Khiyar]:
"Umm al-Khiyar has begun to claim against me a sin, all of which I did not commit."
He meant "lam aṣnaʿhu," and omitted the object. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 4 (part 1 of 3):

There are eighteen issues in this [[So it is in the manuscripts, but the number mentioned is nineteen issues.]]:

The first: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿They ask you what is lawful for them﴾, the verse was revealed concerning 'Adi ibn Hatim and Zayd ibn Muhalhil, who is Zayd al-Khayl, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named Zayd al-Khayr (Zayd of Goodness). They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are a people who hunt with dogs and falcons, and the dogs catch cattle, donkeys and gazelles. Of what they catch, we may reach its slaughter (dhakah, ritual slaughter) in time, and of it, they kill it and we do not reach its slaughter. Allah has forbidden carrion, so what is lawful for us?" Then the verse was revealed.

The second: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿What is lawful for them? Say: Lawful for you are the good things﴾. "Ma" (what) is in the nominative position as the subject, and the predicate is "uhilla lahum" (is lawful for them), and "dha" is superfluous. If you wish, it may mean "alladhi" (that which), and the predicate would be "Say: Lawful for you are the good things," which is the lawful, and everything forbidden is not good. It was said: it is what its eater and drinker enjoys, and there is no harm in it in this world or the Hereafter. It was also said: the good things are the slaughtered animals, because they become good through the dhakah (ritual slaughter).

The third: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and what you have taught﴾, meaning and the game of what you have taught. So there is an ellipsis in the speech which is necessary. Were it not for it, the meaning would require that the lawfulness asked about applies to what is taught from the trained hunting animals (jawarih mukallibin), and that is not the view of anyone. Whoever permits the flesh of the dog does not restrict the permission to the trained one. The rulings of the scholars on eating the dog will come in "al-An'am" [[See vol. 7, p. 115.]], God willing, Exalted is He. Some of those who wrote on the rulings of the Qur'an mentioned that the verse indicates that the permission covers what we have trained from the hunting animals, and this includes the dog and all hunting birds. That requires the permission of all kinds of benefit, so it indicates the permissibility of selling dogs and hunting animals and benefiting from them in all manners of benefit, except what is specified by evidence, which is eating from the hunting animals, meaning predatory dogs and birds of prey. 'Adi had five dogs, which he named with names of distinction. The names of his dogs were Salhab, Ghallab, al-Mukhtalis, and al-Mutana'is. Al-Suhayli said: "And a fifth, I am unsure. Akhtab said it, or Wathhab said it."

The fourth: The community has agreed that if the dog is not black, and a Muslim trains it, then it is sent when it is released, responds when called, desists after catching the game when it is restrained, does not eat from the game it has caught, and has left its mark on it with a wound or by tearing, and a Muslim hunts with it and mentions the name of Allah when releasing it, then its game is sound and may be eaten without disagreement. If any of these conditions is broken, disagreement arises. If what is used for hunting is other than a dog, such as a leopard or the like, or a falcon, a hawk, or similar birds, then the majority of the community holds that whatever it hunts after being trained is a predatory hunter (jarih kasib). It is said: "Jaraha fulan wa-ijtaraha" (so-and-so committed, and he gathered), when he earns. From this comes "al-jariha" (the hunting animal), because by it one earns, and from this comes "ijtiraḥ al-sayyi'at" (committing evil deeds). Al-A'sha said:

"Of a domineering one whose brand is ripened (its wound is burned): it recalls the hunter what he had committed."

[[Al-jabbar: the wasted. Al-maysam: the name for the mark of branding, which is cauterizing. The meaning: the one I satirize keeps my satire visible on him and cannot remove it. The first hemistich in the manuscripts reads "dhat jadd mudhnij maysamuha," and the correction is from "al-Subh al-Munir fi Shi'r Abi Basir."]]

And in the revelation: ﴿He knows what you have committed by day﴾ [[See vol. 7, p. 5.]] (al-An'am 6:60). And He said: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think﴾ [[See vol. 16, p. 165.]] (al-Jathiyah 45:21).

The fifth: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿trained (mukallibin)﴾. The meaning of "mukallibin" is owners of dogs, and it is like "al-mu'addib" (the disciplinarian), the owner of discipline. It was said: its meaning is those who incite (mudhrin) toward game as dogs are incited. Al-Rummani said: both opinions are possible. There is no evidence in "mukallibin" that only dogs are permitted, because it is in the same position as His saying "mu'minin" (believers), even though whoever restricts the permission to dogs alone has relied on it. It is reported from Ibn 'Umar, as Ibn al-Mundhir relates from him, that he said: "As for what is hunted by falcons and other birds, whatever you reach its dhakah, then slaughter it, and it is lawful for you. Otherwise, do not eat it." Ibn al-Mundhir said: Abu Ja'far was asked about the falcon, whether its game is lawful. He said: "No, unless you reach its dhakah." Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: ﴿and what you have taught of the hunting animals, trained﴾ refers to dogs alone. If the dog is black, pure black, then al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Nakha'i disliked its game. Ahmad said: "I do not know anyone who permits it if it is pure black." Ishaq ibn Rahawayh also said this. As for the common scholars of Medina and Kufa, they consider the game of every trained dog permissible. As for those who prohibit the game of the black dog, it is based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The black dog is a devil," narrated by Muslim. The majority argued by the generality of the verse, and they also argued for the permissibility of hunting with the falcon by the reason for revelation mentioned, and by what al-Tirmidhi narrated from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the game of the falcon, and he said: 'What it holds for you, eat.'" In its chain is Mujalid, and it is not known except through him, and he is weak. And by the meaning: whatever can be done by the dog can be done by the leopard, for example, so there is no difference except in what has no bearing on the effect. This is analogy in the meaning of the original, like analogy of the sword to the knife (mudyah), and the female slave to the male slave, and this has already been discussed.

The sixth: And when this is established, know that the hunter must intend at the time of release the dhakah and the permission. This is not disputed, because of the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "If you release your dog and mention the name of Allah over it, then eat." This requires intention and invoking the name. If he intended amusement along with that, Malik disliked it, and Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam permitted it. This is the apparent view of al-Layth's saying: "I have not seen a truth more similar to falsehood than it," meaning hunting. As for doing it without the intention of dhakah, it is forbidden, because it belongs to corruption and the destruction of an animal without benefit, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade killing animals except for food.

The majority of scholars held that naming Allah is necessary by speech at the time of release, because of the saying: "and you mention the name of Allah." If it is not done in any way, the game is not eaten. This is the view of the Zahiris and the group of the people of hadith. Some of our companions and others held that it is permissible to eat what a Muslim hunts and slaughters even if he deliberately omits the naming, and they took the command to name as recommended (nadb). Malik, in the well-known view, distinguished between omitting the naming deliberately or forgetfully. He said: "It is not eaten if omitted deliberately, and it is eaten if omitted forgetfully." This is the saying of the jurists of the cities, and one of al-Shafi'i's two opinions. This issue will come in "al-An'am" [[See vol. 7, p. 75.]], God willing, Exalted is He.

Then there must be the sending of the dog from the hand of the hunter, such that its leash is in his hand, so he releases it and urges it upon the game, and it rushes forth. Or the hunting animal is still while seeing the game, and does not move toward it except by the urging of the hunter. This is in the position of one whose leash is in his hand, and he releases it urging it, according to one of the two opinions. As for if the hunting animal rushes on its own, without release or urging, then its game is not permissible and its meat is not lawful according to the majority, Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion, because it hunted for itself without release, and held the game, and the hunter had no part in it. So its release is not attributed to him, because the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him) does not apply to it: "If you release your trained dog." Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and al-Awza'i said: its game is eaten if it was brought out for hunting.

The seventh: The majority read "'allamtum" with a fatha on the 'ain and the lam. Ibn 'Abbas and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah read it with a damma on the 'ain and a kasra on the lam, meaning from the training of the hunting animals and hunting with them. "Al-jawarih" are the predatory hunters. The limbs of a human being are called "jawarih" because they earn and act. It was also said: they were called "jawarih" because they wound and let blood flow, so it is derived from "al-jirah" (wounds). This view is weak, and the lexicographers are against it, and Ibn al-Mundhir related it from a group. "Mukallibin" is the reading of the majority with a fatha on the kaf and a shadda on the lam. The "mukallib" is the trainer of dogs and the one who incites them [[one who is fond of hunting]]. It is said of one who trains other than dogs: "mukallib," because he returns that animal like the dog. Some have related it. It is also said of the hunter: "mukallib," so according to this its meaning is hunters. It was said: "al-mukallib" is the owner of dogs; it is said: "kallaba, fa-huwa mukallib wa-kallab" (he trained, so he is a trainer and a dog-keeper). Al-Hasan read "muklibin" with a sukun on the kaf and a light lam, and its meaning is owners of dogs. It is said: "amshā al-rajul" (the man's livestock multiplied), and "aklaba" (his dogs multiplied). Al-Asma'i recited, the line is by al-Nabigha, "tukhlijuhu" means "to pull him out":

"And every youth, though he walks and becomes rich, the calamities will snatch him from the world."

**Eighth**: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿You teach them from what Allah has taught you﴾. He used the feminine pronoun, taking into account the wording of *al-jawarih* (the hunting animals), since it is the plural of *jariha* (a hunting animal). There is no disagreement among the scholars regarding two conditions for the teaching: that it obeys when commanded to go (*idha umira*) [In manuscript K: *idha arsala*], and that it desists when called back. There is no disagreement about these two conditions for dogs and what is similar to them among the predatory wild animals. There is disagreement about what is hunted with birds. The well-known view is that these conditions apply to birds according to the majority. Ibn Habib mentioned that the condition of desisting when called back does not apply to birds, since this is generally not possible with them, so it is sufficient that they obey when commanded. Rabi'a said: whatever bird answers when called is the trained (*mu'allam al-ḍari*, a trained and accustomed hunter), because most animals by nature are roused (*yunshali*) [meaning: are incited to pursue]. Al-Shafi'i and the majority of scholars stipulated, as part of the training, that the animal holds the game for its owner, whereas Malik did not stipulate this according to the well-known view from him. Al-Shafi'i said: the trained animal is the one that, when its owner releases it, goes forth, and when he calls it back, returns to him, and holds the game for its owner and does not eat from it. When it does this repeatedly, the people of custom say: it has become trained, and that is the trained animal. It is also reported from al-Shafi'i and the Kufans: if it is released and goes forth, and when it seizes, it holds, and it does this time after time, then its game is eaten on the third occasion. Some scholars said: it does this three times, and its game is eaten on the fourth. Among them is one who said: if it does that once, it is trained, and its game is eaten on the second occasion.

**Ninth**: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿So eat of what they hold for you﴾, meaning: what they have held back for you. The scholars differed in its interpretation. Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayra, al-Nakha'i, Qatada, Ibn Jubayr, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Ikrima, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, al-Nu'man [Abu Hanifa] and his companions said: the meaning is "and it has not eaten." If it eats, then what remains is not to be eaten, because it held for itself and did not hold for its master. According to Abu Hanifa and his companions, the cheetah (*fahd*) is like the dog, and they did not stipulate this for birds; rather, what they eat from is eaten. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abdullah ibn Umar, Salman al-Farisi and Abu Hurayra also said: the meaning is "even if it eats." So when the hunting animal eats, whether it is a dog, a cheetah or a bird, what remains of the game is eaten, even if only a piece is left. This is the view of Malik and all his companions, and it is the second view of al-Shafi'i, and it is the analogical view (*al-qiyas*). In this matter there are two hadiths with the same meaning as what we have mentioned. The first: the hadith of Adi concerning the trained dog ("And if it eats, do not eat, for it has only held for itself"), related by Muslim. The second: the hadith of Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the game of the dog: "If you release your dog and you mention the name of Allah over it, then eat, even if it has eaten from it, and eat what your hand has caught," related by Abu Dawud. It is reported from Adi [a version] which is not authentic, and the authentic one from him is the hadith in Muslim. When the two narrations conflicted, some of our companions and others tried to reconcile them: they took the hadith of prohibition to mean disapproval and scrupulousness (*tanzih* and *wara'*), and the hadith of permission to mean permissibility (*jawaz*). They said: Adi was well-off, so the Prophet (ﷺ) advised him to refrain out of scrupulousness, while Abu Tha'laba was in need, so he advised him permissibility. And Allah knows best. The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the hadith of Adi, "for I fear that it only held for itself," indicates the soundness of this interpretation. This is the interpretation of our scholars. Abu Umar said in *al-Istidhkar*: The hadith of Abu Tha'laba contradicts this hadith of Adi, and it appears that the hadith of Abu Tha'laba abrogates it (*nasikh*). His saying "even if it has eaten" — [Abu Tha'laba] said: "O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Even if it has eaten." I say: This is open to question, because the chronology is unknown, and reconciling the two hadiths is preferable so long as the chronology is not known. And Allah knows best. As for the companions of al-Shafi'i, they said: if the eating is due to extreme hunger on the dog's part, the game is eaten; otherwise it is not eaten, for that is due to poor training. It is also reported from a group of the early generations a distinction between what the dog or cheetah has eaten from, which they prohibited, and what the falcon (*bazi*) has eaten from, which they permitted. This was said by al-Nakha'i, al-Thawri, the people of opinion (*ashab al-ra'y*) and Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and it is related from Ibn Abbas. They said: the dog and the cheetah can be struck and restrained, whereas the bird cannot be treated that way. The limit of its training is that it answers when called and goes forth when released; no more than that can be demanded of it, and striking it would harm it.

**Tenth**: The majority of scholars hold that if the hunting animal drinks blood from the game, the game is still eaten. Ata' said: drinking blood is not eating. Al-Sha'bi and Sufyan al-Thawri disliked eating that game. There is no disagreement among them that the cause of the permissibility of the game, which is the hunting animal's wounding of it, must be certain and not doubtful, and in cases of doubt eating is not permitted.

**Eleventh**: If the hunter finds with his dog another dog, then it is taken to mean that the other dog was not released by another hunter, and that it set off in pursuit of the game by its own nature and inclination. There is no disagreement about this, on the basis of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "And if other dogs have mixed with it, do not eat — in one narration — for you only named your dog and did not name the other." But if another hunter released it, and the two dogs shared in the catch, then the game belongs to the two hunters, who are partners in it. If one of the two dogs inflicted the fatal wound and then the other came, the game belongs to the one that inflicted the fatal wound. Likewise, what is struck by an arrow and then falls from a mountain or drowns in water is not eaten, on the basis of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Adi: "And if you shoot with your arrow, mention the name of Allah. If it disappears from you for a day and you find nothing in it except the trace of your arrow, then eat. But if you find it drowned in water, do not eat, for you do not know whether the water killed it or your arrow." This is an explicit text.

**Twelfth**: If the game dies in the mouths of the dogs without being cut (*bada'*), it is not eaten, because it died by strangulation, and it resembles one slaughtered with a blunt knife which dies during slaughter before its throat is cut. If it was possible for him to take it from the hunting animals and slaughter it, but he did not do so until it died, it is not eaten, and he was negligent in the slaughter, because it had by then become within his power to slaughter it, and the slaughter of what is within one's power differs from the slaughter of what is not within one's power. If he took it and it died before he drew out the knife, or he reached for the knife while it was with him, its eating is permitted. But if the knife was not with him and he busied himself with seeking it, it is not eaten. Al-Shafi'i said: concerning game that the hunting animals have reached but not wounded, there are two opinions. One is that it is not eaten until it is wounded, on the basis of His saying, may He be exalted, "from the hunting animals" [from among the trained predators], and this is the view of Ibn al-Qasim. The other is that it is lawful, and this is the view of Ashhab. Ashhab said: if it dies from the dog's impact, it is eaten.

**Thirteenth**: His saying (ﷺ): "If it disappears from you for a day and you find nothing in it except the trace of your arrow, then eat." A similar wording is found in the hadith of Abu Tha'laba related by Abu Dawud, except that it adds: "Eat it after three days, as long as it has not become putrid." This conflicts with his (ﷺ) saying: "Eat what you have killed outright (*asma'ta*), and leave what has died after going away (*anma'ta*)." *Al-isma'* is what is killed swiftly while you see it; *al-inma'* is when you shoot the game and it disappears from you and dies while you do not see it. It is said: "I have made the shot animal go away (*anmaytu al-ramiyya*), so it went away (*namat*) and then died," when it has disappeared and then died. Imru' al-Qays said:

*"He, his shot prey does not go away, may he not be counted among his clan."*

The scholars differed concerning eating game that disappeared, in three opinions: It is eaten, whether the arrow killed it or the dog did. Second: none of it is to be eaten if it disappeared, on the basis of his saying: "Eat what you have killed outright, and leave what has died after going away."

وَإِنَّمَا لَمْ يُؤْكَلْ مَخَافَةَ أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدْ أَعَانَ عَلَى قَتْلِهِ غَيْرُ السَّهْمِ مِنَ الْهَوَامِّ (creeping or venomous creatures). الثَّالِثُ: الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَ السَّهْمِ فَيُؤْكَلُ وَبَيْنَ الْكَلْبِ فَلَا يُؤْكَلُ، وَوَجْهُهُ أَنَّ السَّهْمَ يَقْتُلُ عَلَى جِهَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَلَا يُشْكِلُ، وَالْجَارِحُ عَلَى جِهَاتٍ مُتَعَدِّدَةٍ فَيُشْكِلُ، وَالثَّلَاثَةُ الْأَقْوَالُ لِعُلَمَائِنَا. وَقَالَ مَالِكٌ فِي غَيْرِ الْمُوَطَّأ (Malik's Muwatta', the early collection of hadith and law): إِذَا بَاتَ الصَّيْدُ ثُمَّ أَصَابَهُ مَيِّتًا لَمْ يُنْفِذِ الْبَازِي أَوِ الْكَلْبُ أَوِ السَّهْمُ مَقَاتِلَهُ لَمْ يَأْكُلْهُ. قَالَ أَبُو عُمَرَ (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr): فَهَذَا يَدُلُّكَ عَلَى أَنَّهُ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَقَاتِلَهُ كَانَ حَلَالًا عِنْدَهُ أَكْلُهُ وَإِنْ بَاتَ، إِلَّا أَنَّهُ يَكْرَهُهُ إِذَا بَاتَ، لِمَا جَاءَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: "وَإِنْ غَابَ عَنْكَ لَيْلَةً فَلَا تَأْكُلْ". وَنَحْوُهُ عَنِ الثَّوْرِيِّ (al-Thawri) قَالَ: إِذَا غَابَ عَنْكَ يَوْمًا كَرِهْتُ أَكْلَهُ. وَقَالَ الشَّافِعِيُّ (al-Shafi'i): الْقِيَاسُ أَلَّا يَأْكُلَهُ إِذَا غَابَ عَنْهُ مَصْرَعُهُ. وَقَالَ الْأَوْزَاعِيُّ (al-Awza'i): إِنْ وَجَدَهُ مِنَ الْغَدِ مَيِّتًا وَوَجَدَ فِيهِ سَهْمَهُ أَوْ أَثَرًا مِنْ كَلْبِهِ فَلْيَأْكُلْهُ. وَنَحْوَهُ قَالَ أَشْهَبُ وَعَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ وَأَصْبَغُ، قَالُوا: جَائِزٌ أَكْلُ الصَّيْدِ وَإِنْ بَاتَ إِذَا نَفَذَتْ مَقَاتِلَهُ. وَقَوْلُهُ فِي الْحَدِيثِ: (مَا لَمْ يُنْتِنْ) تَعْلِيلٌ، لِأَنَّهُ إِذَا أَنْتَنَ لَحِقَ بِالْمُسْتَقْذَرَاتِ الَّتِي تَمُجُّهَا الطِّبَاعُ فَيُكْرَهُ أَكْلُهَا، فَلَوْ أَكَلَهَا لَجَازَ، كَمَا أَكَلَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ الْإِهَالَةَ [[روي أن خياطا دعا النبي ﷺ إلى طعام فقدم إليه إهالة سنخة وخبز شعير. الإهالة: الدسم ما كان، والسنخة: المتغيرة الريح.]] السَّنِخَةَ وَهِيَ الْمُنْتِنَةُ. وَقِيلَ: هُوَ مُعَلَّلٌ بِمَا يُخَافُ مِنْهُ الضَّرَرُ عَلَى آكِلِهِ، وَعَلَى هَذَا التَّعْلِيلِ يَكُونُ أَكْلُهُ مُحَرَّمًا إِنْ كَانَ الْخَوْفُ مُحَقَّقًا، وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

الرَّابِعَةَ عَشْرَةَ: وَاخْتَلَفَ الْعُلَمَاءُ مِنْ هَذَا الْبَابِ فِي الصَّيْدِ بِكَلْبِ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَالنَّصْرَانِيِّ إِذَا كَانَ مُعَلَّمًا، فَكَرِهَهُ الْحَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيُّ. وَأَمَّا كَلْبُ الْمَجُوسِيِّ وَبَازُهُ وَصَقْرُهُ فَكَرِهَ الصَّيْدَ بِهَا جَابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَالْحَسَنُ وَعَطَاءٌ وَمُجَاهِدٌ وَالنَّخَعِيُّ وَالثَّوْرِيُّ وَإِسْحَاقُ. وَأَجَازَ الصَّيْدَ بِكِلَابِهِمْ مَالِكٌ وَالشَّافِعِيُّ وَأَبُو حَنِيفَةَ إِذَا كَانَ الصَّائِدُ مُسْلِمًا، قَالُوا: وَذَلِكَ مِثْلُ شَفْرَتِهِ (his blade, i.e., the knife used in slaughter). وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ الصَّائِدُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ فَجُمْهُورُ الْأُمَّةِ عَلَى جَوَازِ صَيْدِهِ غَيْرَ مَالِكٍ، وَفَرَّقَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ وَبَيْنَ ذَبِيحَتِهِ، وَتَلَا: "يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ تَنَالُهُ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِمَاحُكُمْ" [[راجع ص ٢٩٩ من هذا الجزء.]] ﴿المائدة: ٩٤﴾، قَالَ: فَلَمْ يَذْكُرِ اللَّهُ فِي هَذَا الْيَهُودَ وَلَا النَّصَارَى. وَقَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ وَأَشْهَبُ: صَيْدُ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَالنَّصْرَانِيِّ حَلَالٌ كَذَبِيحَتِهِ. وَفِي كِتَابِ مُحَمَّدٍ: لَا يَجُوزُ صَيْدُ الصَّابِئِ وَلَا ذَبْحُهُ، وَهُمْ قَوْمٌ بَيْنَ الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى وَلَا دِينَ لَهُمْ. وَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ الصَّائِدُ مَجُوسِيًّا فَمَنَعَ مِنْ أَكْلِهِ مَالِكٌ وَالشَّافِعِيُّ وَأَبُو حَنِيفَةَ وَأَصْحَابُهُمْ وَجُمْهُورُ النَّاسِ. وَقَالَ أَبُو ثَوْرٍ فِيهَا قَوْلَانِ: أَحَدُهُمَا كَقَوْلِ هَؤُلَاءِ، وَالْآخَرُ أَنَّ الْمَجُوسَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَأَنَّ صَيْدَهُمْ جَائِزٌ. وَلَوِ اصْطَادَ السَّكْرَانُ أَوْ ذَبَحَ لَمْ يُؤْكَلْ صَيْدُهُ وَلَا ذَبِيحَتُهُ، لِأَنَّ الذَّكَاةَ تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى قَصْدٍ، وَالسَّكْرَانُ لَا قَصْدَ لَهُ.

الْخَامِسَةَ عَشْرَةَ: وَاخْتَلَفَ النُّحَاةُ فِي "مِنْ" فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: "مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ"، فَقَالَ الْأَخْفَشُ: هِيَ زَائِدَةٌ كَقَوْلِهِ: "كُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ" [[راجع ج ٧ ص ٩٩.]] ﴿الأنعام: ١٤١﴾. وَخَطَّأَهُ الْبَصْرِيُّونَ وَقَالُوا: "مِنْ" لَا تُزَادُ فِي الْإِثْبَاتِ وَإِنَّمَا تُزَادُ فِي النَّفْيِ وَالِاسْتِفْهَامِ، وَقَوْلُهُ: "مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ"، "يُكَفِّرُ عَنْكُمْ مِنْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ" [[راجع ج ٣ ص ٣٣٢.]] ﴿البقرة: ٢٧١﴾ و"لِيَغْفِرَ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ" [[راجع ج ١٨ ص ٢٩٩ وص ٨٦.]] ﴿الأحقاف: ٣١﴾ لِلتَّبْعِيضِ. أَجَابَ فَقَالَ: قَدْ قَالَ: "يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ" ﴿نوح: ٤﴾ بِإِسْقَاطِ "مِنْ"، فَدَلَّ عَلَى زِيَادَتِهَا فِي الْإِيجَابِ. أُجِيبَ بِأَنَّ "مِنْ" هَاهُنَا لِلتَّبْعِيضِ، لِأَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا يَحِلُّ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ اللَّحْمُ دُونَ الْفَرْثِ وَالدَّمِ. قُلْتُ: هَذَا لَيْسَ بِمُرَادٍ وَلَا مَعْهُودٍ فِي الْأَكْلِ فَيُعَكِّرُ عَلَى مَا قَالَ. وَيَحْتَمِلُ أَنْ يُرِيدَ "مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ" أَيْ مِمَّا أَبْقَتْهُ الْجَوَارِحُ لَكُمْ، وَهَذَا عَلَى قَوْلِ مَنْ قَالَ: لَوْ أَكَلَ الْكَلْبُ الْفَرِيسَةَ لَمْ يَضُرَّ. وَبِسَبَبِ هَذَا الِاحْتِمَالِ اخْتَلَفَ الْعُلَمَاءُ فِي جَوَازِ أَكْلِ الصَّيْدِ إِذَا أَكَلَ الْجَارِحُ مِنْهُ عَلَى مَا تَقَدَّمَ.

السَّادِسَةَ عَشْرَةَ: وَدَلَّتِ الْآيَةُ عَلَى جَوَازِ اتِّخَاذِ الْكِلَابِ وَاقْتِنَائِهَا لِلصَّيْدِ، وَثَبَتَ ذَلِكَ فِي صَحِيحِ السُّنَّةِ، وَزَادَتِ الْحَرْثَ وَالْمَاشِيَةَ. وَقَدْ كَانَ أَوَّلَ الْإِسْلَامِ أَمْرٌ بِقَتْلِ الْكِلَابِ حَتَّى كَانَ يُقْتَلُ كَلْبُ الْمُرَيَةِ [[المُرَيَة: مصغر المرأة، والأصل المُرَيْئِيَة.]] مِنَ الْبَادِيَةِ يَتْبَعُهَا. رَوَى مُسْلِمٌ عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ: (مَنِ اقْتَنَى كَلْبًا إِلَّا كَلْبَ صَيْدٍ أَوْ مَاشِيَةٍ نَقَصَ مِنْ أَجْرِهِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ قِيرَاطَانِ). وَرُوِيَ أَيْضًا عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: (مَنِ اتَّخَذَ كَلْبًا إِلَّا كَلْبَ مَاشِيَةٍ أَوْ صَيْدٍ أَوْ زَرْعٍ انْتَقَصَ مِنْ أَجْرِهِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ قِيرَاطٌ). قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: وَذُكِرَ لِابْنِ عُمَرَ قَوْلُ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ فَقَالَ: يَرْحَمُ اللَّهُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، كَانَ صَاحِبَ زَرْعٍ. فَقَدْ دَلَّتِ السُّنَّةُ عَلَى مَا ذَكَرْنَا، وَجُعِلَ النَّقْصُ مِنْ أَجْرِ مَنِ اقْتَنَاهَا عَلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْمَنْفَعَةِ، إِمَّا لِتَرْوِيعِ الْكَلْبِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَتَشْوِيشِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ بِنُبَاحِهِ، كَمَا قَالَ بَعْضُ شُعَرَاءِ الْبَصْرَةِ، وَقَدْ نَزَلَ بِعَمَّارٍ فَسَمِعَ لِكِلَابِهِ نُبَاحًا فَأَنْشَأَ يَقُولُ:

نَزَلْنَا بِعَمَّارٍ [[البيت لزيادة الأعجم. وعمار اسم شخص، وروي في (اللسان): أتينا أبا عمرو ... إلخ.]] فَأَشْلَى كِلَابَهُ ... عَلَيْنَا فَكِدْنَا بَيْنَ بَيْتَيْهِ

نُؤْكَلُ فَقُلْتُ لِأَصْحَابِي أُسِرُّ إِلَيْهِمُ ... أَذَا الْيَوْمُ أَمْ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ أَطْوَلُ

(We alighted at the house of 'Ammar, and he set his dogs upon us, and we nearly were devoured between his two houses. I said to my companions, whispering to them: "Is this day longer, or the Day of Resurrection?")

أَوْ لِمَنْعِ دُخُولِ الْمَلَائِكَةِ الْبَيْتَ، أَوْ لِنَجَاسَتِهِ عَلَى مَا يَرَاهُ الشَّافِعِيُّ، أَوْ لِاقْتِحَامِ النَّهْيِ عَنِ اتِّخَاذِ مَا لَا مَنْفَعَةَ فِيهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ. وَقَالَ فِي إِحْدَى الرِّوَايَتَيْنِ: (قِيرَاطَانِ)، وَفِي الْأُخْرَى: (قِيرَاطٌ)، وَذَلِكَ يَحْتَمِلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي نَوْعَيْنِ مِنَ الْكِلَابِ أَحَدُهُمَا أَشَدُّ أَذًى مِنَ الْآخَرِ، كَالْأَسْوَدِ الَّذِي أَمَرَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ بِقَتْلِهِ، وَلَمْ يُدْخِلْهُ فِي الِاسْتِثْنَاءِ حِينَ نَهَى عَنْ قَتْلِهَا فَقَالَ: (عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْأَسْوَدِ الْبَهِيمِ ذِي النُّقْطَتَيْنِ فَإِنَّهُ شَيْطَانٌ)، أَخْرَجَهُ مُسْلِمٌ. وَيَحْتَمِلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ لِاخْتِلَافِ الْمَوَاضِعِ، فَيَكُونُ مُمْسِكُهُ بِالْمَدِينَةِ مَثَلًا أَوْ بِمَكَّةَ يُنْقَصُ قِيرَاطَانِ، وَبِغَيْرِهِمَا قِيرَاطٌ، وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ. وَأَمَّا الْمُبَاحُ اتِّخَاذُهُ فَلَا يَنْقُصُ أَجْرُ مُتَّخِذِهِ، كَالْفَرَسِ وَالْهِرِّ، وَيَجُوزُ بَيْعُهُ وَشِرَاؤُهُ، حَتَّى قَالَ سَحْنُونٌ: وَيَحُجُّ بِثَمَنِهِ. وَكَلْبُ الْمَاشِيَةِ الْمُبَاحُ اتِّخَاذُهُ عِنْدَ مَالِكٍ هُوَ الَّذِي يَسْرَحُ مَعَهَا، لَا الَّذِي يَحْفَظُهَا فِي الدَّارِ مِنَ السُّرَّاقِ. وَكَلْبُ الزَّرْعِ هُوَ الَّذِي يَحْفَظُهُ مِنَ الْوُحُوشِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، لَا مِنَ السُّرَّاقِ. وَقَدْ أَجَازَ غَيْرُ مَالِكٍ اتِّخَاذَهَا لِسُرَّاقِ الْمَاشِيَةِ وَالزَّرْعِ وَالدَّارِ فِي الْبَادِيَةِ.

السَّابِعَةَ عَشْرَةَ: وَفِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ دَلِيلٌ عَلَى أَنَّ الْعَالِمَ لَهُ مِنَ الْفَضِيلَةِ مَا لَيْسَ لِلْجَاهِلِ، لِأَنَّ الْكَلْبَ إِذَا عُلِّمَ يَكُونُ لَهُ فَضِيلَةٌ عَلَى سَائِرِ الْكِلَابِ، فَالْإِنْسَانُ إِذَا كَانَ لَهُ عِلْمٌ أَوْلَى أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ فَضْلٌ عَلَى سَائِرِ النَّاسِ، لَا سِيَّمَا إِذَا عَمِلَ بِمَا عَلِمَ. وَهَذَا كَمَا رُوِيَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ كَرَّمَ اللَّهُ وَجْهَهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قِيمَةٌ، وَقِيمَةُ الْمَرْءِ مَا يُحْسِنُهُ.

الثَّامِنَةَ عَشْرَةَ: قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ أَمْرٌ بِالتَّسْمِيَةِ. قِيلَ: عِنْدَ الْإِرْسَالِ عَلَى الصَّيْدِ، وَفِقْهُ الصَّيْدِ وَالذَّبْحِ فِي مَعْنَى [[من ج وك وز.]] التَّسْمِيَةِ وَاحِدٌ، يَأْتِي بَيَانُهُ فِي "الْأَنْعَامِ" [[راجع ج ٧ ص ٧٥.]]. وَقِيلَ: الْمُرَادُ بِالتَّسْمِيَةِ هُنَا التَّسْمِيَةُ عِنْدَ الْأَكْلِ، وَهُوَ الْأَظْهَرُ. وَفِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ لِعُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ: (يَا غُلَامُ سَمِّ اللَّهَ وَكُلْ بِيَمِينِكَ وَكُلْ مِمَّا يَلِيكَ). وَرُوِيَ مِنْ حَدِيثِ حُذَيْفَةَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: (إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لَيَسْتَحِلُّ الطَّعَامَ إِلَّا يُذْكَرُ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) الْحَدِيثَ. فَإِنْ نَسِيَ التَّسْمِيَةَ أَوَّلَ الْأَكْلِ فَلْيُسَمِّ آخِرَهُ. وَرَوَى النَّسَائِيُّ عَنْ أُمَيَّةَ بْنِ مَخْشِيٍّ، وَكَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ رَأَى رَجُلًا يَأْكُلُ وَلَمْ يُسَمِّ اللَّهَ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي آخِرِ لُقْمَةٍ قَالَ: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ أَوَّلَهُ وَآخِرَهُ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: (مَا زَالَ الشَّيْطَانُ يَأْكُلُ مَعَهُ، فَلَمَّا سَمَّى قَاءَ مَا أَكَلَهُ).

التَّاسِعَةَ عَشْرَةَ: قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ أَمْرٌ بِالتَّقْوَى عَلَى الْجُمْلَةِ، وَالْإِشَارَةُ الْقَرِيبَةُ هِيَ مَا تَضَمَّنَتْهُ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتُ مِنَ الْأَوَامِرِ. وَسُرْعَةُ الْحِسَابِ هِيَ مِنْ حَيْثُ كَوْنُهُ تَعَالَى قَدْ أَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا وَأَحْصَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَدًا، فَلَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى مُحَاوَلَةِ عَدٍّ وَلَا عَقْدٍ كَمَا يَفْعَلُهُ الْحُسَّابُ، وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: "وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ" [[راجع ج ١١ ص ٢٩٣.]] ﴿الأنبياء: ٤٧﴾، فَهُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ يُحَاسِبُ الْخَلَائِقَ دُفْعَةً وَاحِدَةً. وَيَحْتَمِلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ وَعِيدًا بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ، كَأَنَّهُ قَالَ: إِنَّ حِسَابَ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ سَرِيعٌ إِتْيَانُهُ، إِذْ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ قَرِيبٌ. وَيَحْتَمِلُ أَنْ يُرِيدَ بِالْحِسَابِ الْمُجَازَاةَ، فَكَأَنَّهُ تَوَعَّدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا بِمُجَازَاةٍ سَرِيعَةٍ قَرِيبَةٍ إِنْ لَمْ يَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ.

**Ninth issue**? No. This is the first of ten issues (masa'il) in the passage. Here is the translation:

There are ten issues concerning this verse.

**The first issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you﴾. That is, "Today I have perfected your religion for you" and "Today the good things have been made lawful for you." He repeated it for emphasis, meaning: the good things that you asked about have been made lawful for you. The good things had already been permitted to the Muslims before the revelation of this verse, so this is the answer to their question when they said, "What has been made lawful for us?" It was also said that by mentioning "today" He pointed to the time of Muhammad (ﷺ), as one says, "These are the days of so-and-so," meaning this is the time of your ascendancy and the spread of Islam. By this I have perfected your religion, and I have made the good things lawful for you. The good things had already been mentioned in the verse before this one.

**The second issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾. It is a subject (mubtada') and predicate (khabar). The word "food" (ta'am) denotes what is eaten, including slaughtered animals. According to many scholars of exegesis (ta'wil), here it refers specifically to slaughtered animals. As for what is forbidden to us from their food, it does not fall under the general scope of this address. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am: 121], then He made an exception and said: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾, meaning the slaughter of the Jew and the Christian. Even if the Christian says at the slaughter, "In the name of the Messiah," and the Jew says, "In the name of 'Uzayr," that is because they slaughter according to their religion.

'Ata' said: Eat from the slaughter of the Christian even if he says, "In the name of the Messiah," because Allah, mighty and majestic, has permitted their slaughter, and He knows what they say.

Al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymira said: Eat from his slaughter even if he says, "In the name of Sarjis" (the name of a church belonging to them). [Probably the correct reading is Jirjis.] This is also the view of al-Zuhri, Rabi'a, al-Sha'bi and Makhul, and it is narrated from two Companions: Abu al-Darda' and 'Ubada ibn al-Samit.

A group said: If you hear the People of the Book mention other than the name of Allah, mighty and majestic, then do not eat. This view was held among the Companions by 'Ali, 'A'isha and Ibn 'Umar, and it is the view of Tawus and al-Hasan, relying on His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, and indeed it is defiance﴾ [al-An'am: 121].

Malik said: I dislike that, but he did not forbid it.

I say: It is strange that al-Kiya al-Tabari, who reported a consensus on the permissibility of the slaughter of the People of the Book, then went on to argue from this that mentioning the name of Allah over the slaughtered animal is not a condition. He said: There is no doubt that they do not mention over the slaughtered animal anything but a god who is not truly worshipped, such as the Messiah and 'Uzayr. If they mentioned the true God, their mention would not be in the manner of worship, but in some other way. And requiring the mention of the name when it is not in the manner of worship makes no sense. The mention of the name by a disbeliever and its absence are on the same footing, when worship cannot be conceived of from him. And because the Christian slaughters in the name of the Messiah, and Allah has ruled the lawfulness of their slaughter absolutely. In that is evidence that mentioning the name is not a condition at all, as al-Shafi'i says. The views of the scholars on this will come in "al-An'am," God willing.

**The third issue:** There is no disagreement among the scholars that what does not need ritual slaughter (dhaka), such as food that involves no processing, like fruit and wheat, is permissible to eat, since no one's ownership harms it. Food that involves processing is of two kinds. The first is what involves a craft unrelated to religion, such as grinding flour, pressing oil and the like. If such food is avoided when it comes from a dhimmi (a protected non-Muslim), it is out of disgust. The second kind is slaughter (tadhkiyah), which we mentioned requires religion and intention. Since the analogy would be that their slaughter is not permissible, just as we say they have no valid prayer and no accepted worship, Allah has granted a concession regarding their slaughter to this community, and the text has taken it out of the analogy, as we have mentioned from the saying of Ibn 'Abbas. And Allah knows best.

**The fourth issue:** The scholars also differed over whether the slaughter performed by them is effective for what is forbidden to them, on two views. The majority hold that it is effective for the entire animal, what is lawful for them and what is forbidden to them, because it has been ritually slaughtered (mudhakkan). But a group of scholars said: What is lawful to us from their slaughter is only what is lawful to them, because what is not lawful to them, their slaughter does not affect. So this group prohibited the tarif [a Hebrew term; in al-Kharashi's commentary on Mukhtasar Khalil, it means: that the slaughtered animal is found with a diseased lung, i.e., stuck to the animal's back. The method was forbidden to them because that is a sign that the animal would not live, so slaughter is not effective on it according to them, comparable to a pierced vital organ according to us], and the pure fats from the slaughter of the People of the Book, and they restricted the word "food" to part of it. The first group took it in its general sense for everything that is eaten.

This disagreement also exists in the school of Malik. Abu 'Umar said: Malik disliked the fats of the Jews and eating what they slaughtered of camels, while most scholars do not see any harm in that. This will come in "al-An'am," God willing. Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, disliked what they slaughter when a Muslim's slaughter is available, and he disliked that they have markets in which they sell what they slaughter. This, from him, may Allah have mercy on him, was an act of scrupulousness.

**The fifth issue:** As for the Magians (al-Majus), the scholars agree, except for those who deviated, that their slaughter may not be eaten and that one may not marry from them, because they are not People of the Book according to the well-known position among the scholars. There is no harm in eating the food of those who have no scripture, such as polytheists and idol worshippers, as long as it is not from their slaughter and does not need ritual slaughter, except cheese, because of the rennet (infaha) of carrion in it. [Rennet (infaha), with the hamza vowelled with a kasra and the fa' with a fatha: the stomach of a suckling lamb or kid as long as it has not eaten. Once it has eaten it becomes a stomach, from which is extracted a yellowish substance placed in milk so that it curdles.]

If the father of a child is a Magian and his mother is a Christian or Jew, his ruling is the ruling of his father according to Malik. According to others, the slaughter of a child is not eaten if either of his parents is one whose slaughter is not eaten.

**The sixth issue:** As for the slaughter of the Christians of the tribe of Banu Taghlib and the slaughter of any newcomer into Judaism or Christianity, 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used to forbid the slaughter of the Banu Taghlib, because they are Arabs, and he said: They have not adhered to anything of Christianity except drinking wine. This is also the view of al-Shafi'i. On this basis, what is forbidden is not the slaughter of the genuine Christians among them.

The majority of the community said: The slaughter of every Christian is lawful, whether he is from the Banu Taghlib or from others, and likewise the Jew. Ibn 'Abbas argued with His saying: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 51]. If the Banu Taghlib were not Christians except by their allegiance to them, their slaughter would be eaten.

**The seventh issue:** There is no harm in eating, drinking and cooking in the vessels of all the disbelievers, as long as they are not gold or silver, or pig skin, after being washed and boiled, because they do not guard against impurities and eat carrion. If they cook in those pots, they become impure, and impurities may seep into the parts of earthenware pots; if food is cooked in them afterwards, there is a possibility of those impure parts mixing with what is cooked in the pot a second time, so caution requires abstaining from them.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: If the vessel is of copper or iron, it is washed; if it is of earthenware, water is boiled in it, then it is washed. This applies when it is needed. Malik also said this. As for what they use for other than cooking, there is no harm in using it without washing, because of what al-Daraqutni narrated from 'Umar, that he performed ablution from the house of a Christian, from a box (haqq) belonging to a Christian woman. [The haqq and haqqa (with a damma): a container made of wood or ivory.] It is authentic, and it will come in "al-Furqan" in full.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Tha'laba al-Khushani, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are in the land of a people of the Book; we eat in their vessels, and we are in a land of game. I hunt with my bow, I hunt with my trained dog, and I hunt with my dog that is not trained. Inform me what is lawful for us of that?" He said: (As for what you mentioned, that you are in the land of a people of the Book and eat in their vessels: if you find other than their vessels, do not eat in them; and if you do not find any, wash them and then eat in them.) Then he mentioned the hadith.

**The eighth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your food is lawful for them﴾. This is evidence that they are addressed with the details of our law: if they buy meat from us, the meat is lawful for them, and the price taken from them is lawful for us.

**The ninth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the chaste women from among the believing women and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, to the end of the verse. Its meaning has already been mentioned in "al-Baqara" [vol. 3, p. 69 onwards] and "al-Nisa'" [vol. 5, p. 120], and praise is to Allah.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture﴾, that it refers to those under a covenant, not those in the land of war, so it is specific. Others said: It is permissible to marry dhimmi women and women from the land of war, because of the generality of the verse.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The chaste women" are the modest women who are sound of mind. Al-Sha'bi said: It means that she guards her chastity so she does not commit adultery, and that she performs the ritual bath from major impurity. Al-Sha'bi recited "wal-muhsinat" with a kasra on the sad, and al-Kisa'i also recited it that way. Mujahid said: "Al-muhsanat" means free women. Abu 'Ubayd said: He holds that it is not lawful to marry the slave women of the People of the Book, because of His saying: ﴿So from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [al-Nisa': 25]. This is the view held by the majority of the scholars.

**The tenth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith﴾. It was said: When He, exalted is He, said, "the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture," the women of the People of the Book said: "If Allah, exalted is He, were not pleased with our religion, He would not have permitted you to marry us." So the verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith﴾, meaning in what was sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Abu al-Haytham said: The "ba'" (in bil-iman) is redundant, meaning: whoever disbelieves the faith, that is, denies it, ﴿then his deed has become worthless﴾. Ibn al-Sumayqa recited "faqad habita" with a fatha on the ba'.

It was also said: When obligations and rulings that must be upheld were mentioned, the threat against violating them was mentioned, because of what that contains of emphasizing the deterrent against neglecting them.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid that the meaning is: whoever disbelieves in Allah. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: If this narration is authentic, its meaning is "by the Lord of the faith."

Shaykh Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari said: It is not permissible to call Allah "faith" (iman), contrary to the Hashwiyya and the Salimiyya, because iman is the verbal noun of "amana, yu'minu, iman," its active participle is mu'min, and iman is affirmation (tasdiq); affirmation is only speech, and the Creator, exalted is He, cannot be speech.

[Note found on a page in the handwriting of the author, from here to the end of the page: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith, then his deed has become worthless﴾. The scholars: that is, the reward of his deed and its recompense, because disbelief, though it occurs, God forbid, and nullifies what preceded of his faith, does not turn existence from him into non-existence from its root. Rather, it nullifies his reward and voids his recompense. And the consensus of the Muslims on establishing apostasy indicates that faith existed before it. Thus it is clear by this that disbelief, when it befalls faith, cuts it off from the moment it occurs onward; his reward is nullified, not that its essence is nullified so that it becomes as if it never was, and what existed becomes in reality counted as non-existent. This is clear, and Allah knows best.]

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 1 of 8)**

It contains thirty-two issues.

**The first issue:** Al-Qushayri and Ibn Atiyya mention that this verse was revealed concerning the incident of ʿAʾishah when she lost her necklace during the expedition of al-Muraysi. It is the verse of the ablution (wudu') [a ritual washing before prayer]. Ibn Atiyya said: "However, since the ablution was already established and in use among them, the verse only added to them its recitation, and it gave them the benefit and the concession of tayammum [dry ablution with clean earth]. We have mentioned in the verse of *al-Nisa'* [[See vol. 5, p. 214.]] a view contrary to this, and Allah knows best." The meaning of this verse falls within what was commanded regarding fulfilling contracts and the rulings of the Sharia, and within what was mentioned regarding the completion of His blessing, for this concession is among the completions of blessings.

**The second issue:** The scholars differed over the intended meaning of His words ﴿When you rise to prayer﴾, according to several opinions. One group said: this is a general expression applying to every rising to prayer, whether the one rising is in a state of purity or in a state of minor impurity (ḥadath). Thus, whenever he rises to prayer, he should perform ablution. ʿAli used to do this and recite this verse. This was mentioned by Abu Muhammad al-Darimi [[al-Darimi (with a kasra on the letter ra): attributed to Darim, a clan of Tamim.]] in his *Musnad*. Something similar is related from ʿIkrimah. Ibn Sirin said: "The caliphs used to perform ablution for every prayer."

I say: On this view, the verse is *muhkam* (definitive, not abrogated) and there is no abrogation (naskh) in it.

Another group said: the address is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ). ʿAbdullah ibn Handhalah ibn Abi ʿAmir al-Ghasil [[Thus in the originals. Al-Ghasil is Handhalah (may Allah be pleased with him), who heard the call to battle while in a state of major impurity, so he was martyred, and the angels washed him.]] said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to perform ablution for every prayer, and this was difficult for him, so he was commanded to use the miswak, and the ablution was lifted from him except for a minor impurity."

ʿAlqamah ibn al-Faghwa related from his father, who was one of the Companions and was the guide of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Tabuk: "This verse was revealed as a concession for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because he did not perform any act without being in a state of ablution, and he would not speak to anyone or return a greeting, and so on. So Allah informed him through this verse that the ablution is only for rising to prayer, and not for the rest of the actions."

Another group said: the verse means ablution for every prayer, seeking additional merit (fadl). They understood the command as recommendation (nadb). Many of the Companions, including Ibn ʿUmar, used to perform ablution for every prayer seeking merit, and the Prophet (ﷺ) used to do this until, on the day of the Conquest, he combined the five prayers with one ablution, intending to make clear to his community (ﷺ).

I say: The apparent meaning of this view is that performing ablution for every prayer, before the revelation of the abrogating text, was recommended and not obligatory. This is not so, for when a command is revealed, its requirement is obligation, especially according to the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, as is well known from their conduct.

Others said: the obligation regarding every ablution was for every prayer, and then it was abrogated at the Conquest of Makkah. This is an error, because of the hadith of Anas who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to perform ablution for every prayer, while his community was not in this practice," and this will come later. Also, [there is] the hadith of Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿman that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed ʿAsr and Maghrib at al-Sahbaʾ [[al-Sahbaʾ: a location near Khaybar.]] with one ablution, and that was during the expedition of Khaybar, which was in the sixth year; it was also said the seventh year, and the Conquest of Makkah was in the eighth year. This is a sound hadith, related by Malik in his *Muwatta'*, and recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim. By these two hadiths it becomes clear that the obligation to perform ablution for every prayer did not exist before the Conquest.

If it is said: Muslim related from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb [[In Usd al-Ghabah: al-Husayb, with a dammah on the unmarked letter and a fathah on the sad.]] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to perform ablution for every prayer, and when the day of the Conquest came, he prayed the prayers with one ablution and wiped over his leather socks. ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "You did something today that you were not doing." He said: "I did it intentionally, O ʿUmar." Why did ʿUmar ask him and inquire? It is answered: he asked him only because he had departed from his usual practice since praying at Khaybar, and Allah knows best.

Al-Tirmidhi related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to perform ablution for every prayer, whether in a state of purity or not. Humayd said: "I asked Anas: 'How did you used to do it?' He said: 'We used to perform one ablution.'" He said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." It is also related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Ablution upon ablution is light." So he (peace be upon him) used to renew his ablution for every prayer. He (peace be upon him) was greeted while he was urinating and did not return the greeting until he performed tayammum, and then he returned the greeting and said: "I disliked mentioning Allah except in a state of purity." This was related by al-Daraqutni.

Al-Suddi and Zayd ibn Aslam said: the meaning of the verse ﴿When you rise to prayer﴾ is: "rising from your beds," meaning from sleep. The purpose of this interpretation is to include the minor impurities in the mention, especially sleep, which is disputed as to whether it is itself a minor impurity or not. On this interpretation, there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse. The intended meaning is: "O you who believe, when you rise to prayer from sleep, or when one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have touched women—meaning the minor touch—then wash," so the rulings of one in a state of minor impurity (ḥadath aṣghar) are complete. Then He said: ﴿And if you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves﴾; this is the ruling of another category. Then He said regarding both categories together: ﴿And if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then take clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it﴾ [al-Nisa': 43]. This interpretation was adopted by Muhammad ibn Maslamah, from the companions of Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, and others.

The majority of scholars said: the meaning of the verse is: "When you rise to prayer while in a state of minor impurity." On this view there is no inversion in the verse; rather, the ruling of the one who finds water is ordered up to His words ﴿then purify yourselves﴾, and the minor touch is included in His words "in a state of minor impurity." Then, after His words ﴿And if you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves﴾, He mentioned the ruling of the one who lacks water in both categories together. The touching was intercourse, and it is necessary that the one in major impurity who lacks water be mentioned just as the one who finds water was mentioned. This is the interpretation of al-Shafiʿi and others, and the statements of the Companions, such as Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, Ibn ʿAbbas, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and others, agree with it.

I say: These two interpretations are the best of what has been said regarding the verse, and Allah knows best.

The meaning of ﴿When you rise﴾ is "when you intend," as the Exalted said: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge [with Allah]﴾ [al-Nahl: 98], i.e., when you intend to recite, because performing ablution at the very moment of rising to prayer is not possible.

**The third issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿wash your faces﴾. He mentioned four limbs: the face, whose obligation is washing; the hands likewise; the head, whose obligation is wiping, by consensus; and the feet, about which there is disagreement, as will come. Nothing other than these was mentioned, and this indicates that whatever is other than these is etiquette (adab) and recommended practices (sunan). And Allah knows best.

In washing the face, it is necessary to bring water to it and to pass the hand over it, and this is the real meaning of washing according to us. We have explained this in *al-Nisa'* [[See vol. 5, pp. 209 onward.]]. Others among us said: it is only required to make the water flow over it, and there is no requirement to rub it with the hand. There is no doubt that if a man immerses himself in water and dips his face or his hand without rubbing, it is said that he washed his face and his hand, and it is known that in this there is no requirement beyond the occurrence of the name; when that occurs, it suffices.

The word "face" (wajh) in the language is derived from "confronting" (muwajahah), and it is a limb that comprises parts and has length and breadth. Its boundary in length is from the beginning of the surface of the forehead to the end of the two jaws, and in breadth from ear to ear. This is for a beardless man. As for a bearded man, when the chin is covered with hair, it is either thin or thick. If the first, so that the skin can be seen through it, it is necessary to let the water reach the skin. If it is thick, the obligation has shifted to it, like the hair of the head.
